Wall Street's post-election rally lasted exactly one day.

U.S. stocks plunged Thursday, Nov. 5, in a ferocious sell-off in technology and artificial intelligence shares, according to Reuters. The Nasdaq fell 5.5%, the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, and the Dow fell 3.4%, with all 11 S&P sectors ending lower. Technology shares fell 7.3%, and the Philadelphia chip index fell 12% — its second-biggest drop on record. About $2 trillion was wiped off the Nasdaq in a single day.

The losses were concentrated in the AI trade that had powered the market for two years. Nvidia shares sank 9.3%, Advanced Micro Devices plunged 17.3%, and CoreWeave, which rents access to AI chips through the cloud, lost 9.8%, according to the Associated Press. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,833 points.

Why it happened — and what it means here

The sell-off came one day after Democrats swept the midterm elections, taking control of the House and Senate. President Donald Trump blamed the election results for the plunge, writing on Truth Social that the market "suffered one of the Worst Days in History based on the results of the Election."

Analysts pointed to a different mix of causes: stretched AI valuations, worries that Democratic victories could slow data center construction, and a broader reassessment of the AI buildout. AI stocks fell in part on fears that new Democratic governors and legislators — including Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who has pledged to regulate data centers more tightly — could put new limits on the industry.

That debate lands directly on Texas. The state has become a hub for data center construction, and Gov. Greg Abbott paused new data center permits earlier this fall, as Webb Watch 956 previously reported. The 90th Texas Legislature convenes January 12, and how the new governor and lawmakers handle data centers, power demand, and water use will shape the industry's future in the state.

For Laredo readers, the immediate effect is in retirement accounts: sharp single-day drops hit 401(k)s and IRAs invested in broad market funds. The market had rallied Wednesday in the first session after the election, before reversing violently Thursday.

title: Tech Stocks Plunge a Day After the Election as the AI Rally Unravels
